subject: Sizing for Navisys private GPU pool — throughput targets & scaling options
messages:
From: Sam Wong <sam.wong@navisys.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.example
Date: 2026-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private GPU pool sizing — initial numbers

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. As a follow-up, I’m sending our rough load profile and a couple of constraints so Redwood can recommend a sizing approach for a private (VPC) deployment. Attached: navisys-loadprofile.csv and a network sketch (navisys-network-diagram.png).

Quick background: we run a customer-facing AI assistant that generates multi-turn answers. Typical request payloads average ~900 tokens (prompt + context) and the model we're evaluating produces ~1.2k tokens on average. Our target SLO is p95 latency <= 400ms for first 64 tokens and p95 latency <= 700ms for full response on steady-state traffic.

Traffic outline (from the CSV):
- Sustained baseline: ~80 QPS
- Daily peak: 220 QPS (10–15 minute bursts)
- Occasional spikes: up to 380 QPS (rare, 2–3 times per week, 5–10 minutes)
- Concurrency per tenant: often 650 concurrent streams at peak

Operational constraints:
- All inference must stay inside our VPC (no egress to hosted Redwood).
- Sensitive tenants need isolation lanes (dedicated GPU carve-outs).
- We prefer predictable unit costs and an autoscaling plan that avoids noisy neighbor impact.

Can you provide a first-pass sizing and a list of questions/data points you need from us to tighten estimates? Also flag networking and NIC considerations — we have 100Gbps fabric between hosts and single 40Gbps uplinks from racks (diagram attached).

Cheers,
Sam Wong
Head of Platform — Navisys

Hi Sam — thanks for the profile and diagram, that’s very helpful. Looping in Karthik (capacity modeling) and Jonas (network/infra) to draft a sizing sketch.

High-level notes and assumptions we’ll start from (please confirm):
- Generator model: please confirm exact family & parameterization (e.g., Llama-2-70B/opt-family/other). Throughput varies hugely by architecture and optimizations (fused kernels / quantization).
- Tokenization: are the 900 / 1.2k token figures measured post-tokenizer?
- Warm KV cache behavior: what fraction of requests are served with long context reuse (prefix cache hit rate)?
- Persistence: do you need model state persisted per-tenant between requests?

Initial ask: if you can confirm the model family and attach a short sample of request/response pairs (anonymized), that will tighten our numbers.

We’ll produce a readiness checklist (network egress rules, instance types, suggested lane sizes, warmup strategy, and autoscale policy) and an initial capacity sketch by Wed EOD PST.

Next steps: I’ll convert the notes into a short Mutual Action Plan with milestones (PO, infra handoff, pilot).

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.example, Sam Wong <sam.wong@navisys.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.example
Date: 2026-05-18T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool sizing — initial numbers

Hi team — I ran a quick first-pass model based on the CSV and the latency targets. Below are engineering assumptions and the resulting sizing scenarios. This is a back-of-envelope; we’ll refine with model-family and tokenization detail.

Assumptions we used for the sketch:
- Model class: high-capacity transformer (approx equivalent perf to 70B FP16 / quant-friendly)
- Average generation: 1.2k output tokens; effective per-request work ~2.1k tokens including input
- Batch efficiency: steady-state batching yields ~2.5x throughput improvement vs naive single-stream execution; bursts reduce batching efficiency (assume 1.4x during spikes)
- KV/prefix cache: assume 35% effective cache hit for steady-state; for isolated tenants the hit may be higher if session affinity is enabled
- Target p95 latency budget: 400ms for first 64 tokens (we budget ~200–250ms in compute, remainder for queueing & network)

Sizing scenarios (lane = a set of GPUs serving a tenant slice; we propose multiple lanes to isolate noisy tenants):
- Conservative (aim for p95 SLO under spikes): 6 lanes x 4 x A100-80GB GPUs (24 GPUs total). Expected sustained throughput: ~260 QPS at steady batching; handles up to ~360 QPS with degraded batching but within p95 target if KV cache warm.
- Cost-optimized (accept occasional p95 degradation during extreme spikes): 4 lanes x 4 x A100-80GB GPUs (16 GPUs). Expected sustained throughput: ~170 QPS; burst headroom to ~260 QPS with slower tails on p95.

Network and host considerations:
- PCIe and NVLink topology: prefer hosts with 3+ NVLinks per GPU to reduce cross-device shuffling for attention-kernel heavy workloads.
- NIC: allocate 100Gbps per host for cross-rack traffic during model downloads, KV syncs, and large-batch responses. If you only have 40Gbps uplinks per rack, ensure burst queueing at the top-of-rack and avoid colocating all lanes in a single rack.
- Egress: if customer keeps logs in their VPC, budget for 1.2k tokens response * 380 QPS peak = ~570 Mbps uncompressed; multiply by RTTs and replication if you mirror logs to s3.

Autoscale recommendations:
- Multi-tier autoscale: 1) fast short-term vertical scale via batch window widening (short-term response latency may increase slightly), 2) horizontal pod scale (add GPUs) on sustained load >5 min, 3) cold-fallback policy to a smaller model variant for extreme spikes.

Operational notes:
- Warmup: maintain a small warm pool per lane to keep KV warmed and avoid cold-start spikes in latency.
- Isolation: map sensitive tenants to dedicated lanes with pinning to specific GPUs; split RBAC and KMS at lane boundaries.

I’ll convert these into a one-page sizing matrix and include a cost-band estimate for A100 vs cheaper Ampere options in the full doc.

-Karthik
Senior Capacity Engineer — Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- Model family: we are testing with a quantized 70B-family variant (optimized kernels, 4-bit quant). We expect equivalently higher per-GPU throughput than FP16 but want to be conservative.
- Token counts: our numbers are post-tokenizer. We’ll share a sample anon request set by EOD.
- Cache behavior: about 40% prefix reuse for the assistant flows, but some tenants see >70% during session-heavy windows.
- Rack topology: each rack has a 40Gbps uplink; top-of-rack switches are dual-homed to a 100Gbps spine. We tried to show this in the attached diagram.

Additional ask: Navisys wants a recommended pilot configuration we can stand up quickly (2–4 week pilot) that demonstrates both steady-state and burst handling and includes the isolation lane for PII-heavy tenants. Also include an ops playbook for when p95 degrades past target (runbook steps).

Can you include a short estimate (monthly infra cost + Redwood private runtime fee) for the conservative vs cost-optimized lanes so we can present to procurement next week?

Sam

Subject: Re: Private GPU pool sizing — initial numbers

Sam — thanks for the clarifications and the sample data set (we received it). Summary and next actions below.

Summary (agreed assumptions):
- Model: quantized 70B-family, measured token counts are post-tokenizer.
- Warm cache hit: average 40%; some tenants 70%+ (we will map high-hit tenants to smaller dedicated lanes).
- Network: 40Gbps rack uplinks, dual-homed to 100Gbps spine (good to know — we’ll recommend cross-rack placement for lanes to avoid saturating a single rack).

Pilot proposal (2–4 week):
- Minimal pilot topology: 2 lanes, each lane = 4 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (8 GPUs total). One lane pinned for PII tenants (isolation + KMS).
- Objectives: validate sustained 100–140 QPS with p95 latency targets, test burst handling to 300 QPS for short windows, validate autoscale hysteresis and cache warmup policy.
- Metrics to capture: per-lane p50/p95/p99 latency, batch size distribution, KV hit rate, PCIe/NVLink utilization, host NIC utilization, and cold-start incidence.

Runbook highlights (short):
1) Detect: alert when lane p95 > 1.2x target for 3 consecutive 1-min windows.
2) Immediate mitigation: increase batch window by 25ms, momentary deprioritization of non-PII lanes, and trigger a horizontal scale event if sustained >5 min.
3) Escalation: if p95 remains degraded after scale, fallback to smaller model variant and open incident.

Rough commercial-band estimate (monthly, infra-only):
- Conservative lane set (24 GPUs total): infra ~$125k/mo; Redwood private runtime fee (including 24/7 support & observability) ~$34k/mo.
- Cost-optimized lane set (16 GPUs total): infra ~$84k/mo; Redwood fee ~$24k/mo.

Next steps: we’ll assemble a one-page mutual action plan with milestones (pilot sign, infra handoff, pilot execution, evaluation) and send a formal PO template. If that sounds good I’ll schedule a 30-min pilot kickoff with our infra on Mon.

Thanks — we’ll attach the one-page sizing matrix and the runbook in the MAP doc.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
